rows.notes: The paper is explicitly a review ('a review of 10 years of research in Kansas'); the Procedures section states it summarizes several KSU studies and refers readers to the cited references (Lamm et al. 1995a, Caldwell et al. 1994, Lamm et al. 1997a,b, O'Brien et al. 1998) for data and methods. The yield, water-use and economic results supporting feasibility/profitability of SDI corn (12.5 Mg/ha yields with ~25% less net irrigation; SDI cost-competitive with center pivot for 10-20 year system life and smaller fields, Fig. 5 adapted from O'Brien et al. 1998) are re-reported from those earlier publications, so they are not counted as this paper's own results. The only material that may be newly reported here is the long-term zone flow-rate monitoring 1989-1998 (Fig. 6), which concerns system longevity rather than profitability directly. Under the rule that reviews are 'no' on Q1, all questions are answered 'no'; the claim itself (feasible and profitable SDI corn in Kansas) is consistent with what the review summarizes, but the primary evidence lies in the cited KSU papers.

notes: Document is a self-review by the same research group of their 1989-1999 SDI corn program at Colby and Garden City, Kansas; text appears complete. The Texas part of the claim is attributed to Howell et al. (1997), not this paper.
